title: Dative Basics
definition: The dative case is commonly used for the indirect object—the person receiving or benefiting from something—and after certain verbs and prepositions. In basic article forms, masculine der becomes dem, feminine die becomes der, neuter das becomes dem, and plural die becomes den (usually with -n added to the noun when possible).

rules.title: Dative articles
rules.explanation: Memorize the dative forms of definite articles: der → dem, die → der, das → dem, plural die → den. For indefinite articles, ein becomes einem (masculine/neuter) and eine becomes einer (feminine).

rules.title: Indirect object: to whom?
rules.explanation: A dative object often identifies the person receiving something. Ask wem? (to whom?/for whom?) to help identify it.

examples.german: Ich gebe dem Mann das Buch.
examples.english: I give the man the book.
examples.note: Wem gebe ich das Buch? — dem Mann.

examples.german: Wir schenken dem Kind einen Ball.
examples.english: We give the child a ball as a gift.

rules.title: Indefinite and possessive articles
rules.explanation: In the dative, common forms include einem, einer, meinem, meiner, deinem, deiner, and plural meinen. The ending depends on the noun's gender and number.

rules.title: Common dative verbs
rules.explanation: Some frequent verbs take the dative even when English does not use 'to'. Learn these as fixed patterns: helfen, danken, gefallen, gehören.

examples.english: I like that. / That appeals to me.
The book belongs to my friend.

rules.title: Common dative prepositions
rules.explanation: These prepositions always take the dative: aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu. A useful mnemonic is 'aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu'.

examples.english: I am at my friend's place.
We are going to the doctor.

examples.german: Er wohnt seit einem Jahr hier.
examples.english: He has lived here for one year.

common_mistakes.explanation: Bus is masculine; mit always takes the dative.
Kind is neuter singular, so use dem.
Danken takes the dative pronoun dir.

memorization_list.english: dative masculine and neuter definite article

memorization_list.german: aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu

mastery_goal: You can recognize basic dative objects, use common dative article forms, and remember frequent dative verbs and prepositions.
